title: Everything built: the full redesign plus checklists, guides and AI labels

steps.headline: Home: search button top right, "Popular alternatives", trimmed text.
steps.changed: The search box in the top bar is now just a magnifier button on every non-search page.
steps.notice: Less clutter at the top of every page.

steps.headline: Phones get a liquid-glass tab bar: Home · Browse · Search · Gaps.
steps.changed: Boards is gone from the tabs; Browse jumps to the categories.
steps.notice: Tabs and Sign in are translucent.

steps.headline: Group page: breadcrumb, "Talk about this on r/TrueOpenSource", and new Must have and Cards/Compare controls.
steps.changed: The boards section is gone; "Most voted" is now a sort option.
steps.notice: Each card has a Features fold.

steps.headline: "Must have" lets you tick several features; only projects that do all of them stay.
steps.changed: Each item shows how many projects say yes.
steps.notice: Unknown answers don't count as a match.
steps.risk: Some big projects still have unknown answers, so they drop out when filtered.

steps.headline: Compare shows every project against the group's checklist side by side.
steps.changed: Tap a cell for its note and source.
steps.risk: LibreOffice still has blanks (see the question at the end).

steps.headline: On phones the compare table scrolls sideways with the names fixed.
Each card has a closed "Features" fold listing its checklist answers.
steps.changed: Out of the card's main area, as you asked.

steps.headline: On phones the same controls sit in one row.
Project page with breadcrumb, back button and the AI-contribution line in How to help.
On phones every section folds closed except the header.
steps.changed: Family, Screenshots, Listed in, Features, How to help.

steps.headline: A project's Features card shows each checklist answer with its note and source.
steps.notice: Sources link to the project's own pages.

steps.headline: "AI Contributions: Non-developers welcome" opens the project's own rule, outside help and where to start.
Projects that stopped taking outside code say so plainly.
steps.changed: "Not accepting outside code" with their own words.

steps.path: A project with no written rule
steps.headline: Projects with no rule say "Not stated yet. Maintainers can set this by claiming the listing."
steps.notice: About 2 in 3 projects show this for now.

steps.headline: "Switching from Google Docs": how to get your data out, what you get, what won't come over, and what opens it.
steps.changed: 110 apps have a guide so far.
steps.notice: Steps link to the vendor's own help page.

steps.headline: On phones the switch guide is a fold at the top.
Search page: one full-width bar with a Filter button inside it.
steps.changed: Type, Works on (several) and Setup in one menu.

steps.headline: On phones the match label sits top right and titles cut off with "…".
The phone filter is a full-width sheet with a handle, anchored to the edges.
Most requested: top three large, the rest in two columns numbered down.
On phones all requests stack; the number sits beside the name.
New: "Missing everywhere" and "Only partly anywhere", built from the checklists.
steps.changed: e.g. Video editing: no phone app anywhere.

steps.headline: Claim your project: one short line and one Sign in button.
steps.notice: Big projects need a mod's confirmation.

steps.headline: How should the remaining blank checklist answers be filled?
steps.today: About 2,100 answers are filled, each backed by a quote from the project's own pages. Many big projects still have blanks (LibreOffice Writer: live co-editing and Word files) because their help sites block automated reading.
steps.problem: Blank cells on the best-known projects make the compare table look broken, and those projects drop out of "Must have" filters.

options.label: Fill well-known facts
pros: Fills the obvious ones now (LibreOffice works offline; no live co-editing on the desktop app).
Each answer still links to the project's site.
cons: No exact quote behind those answers; a few may be wrong until corrected.

options.label: Read sites in a real browser
cons: Slower; some sites (Mozilla, Fedora) still block it.

options.label: Leave blanks
cons: Thin tables on the biggest projects.

steps.path: Projects owned by a GitHub organisation
steps.headline: For organisation projects, is a mod checking by eye enough for now?
steps.today: Personal projects are proven automatically. For organisation projects the claimant must make their membership public, add a small file, and a mod confirms.
steps.problem: GitHub doesn't publicly say who owns an organisation, so the site can't check it alone.
steps.proposal: Keep the mod check for now. A fully automatic check needs a GitHub App installed on each organisation, or an extra GitHub permission from the claimant.

steps.path: A new last step: "How you'd like help"
steps.headline: Add the contributor-preferences step to claiming?
steps.today: Developers can write a pitch, nothing more.
steps.problem: Newcomers (especially with AI tools) can't tell how a project wants help.
steps.proposal: Seven quick questions, about two minutes, pre-filled from their own files: AI contributions (your four labels), how to start, help wanted most (incl. co-maintainers), newcomers welcome?, how to say AI helped, anything to sign, how fast they review. Shown as one line in the card fold, rows under How to help, and a "Contributing" filter. Answers go live right away; only new links wait for a mod.
